title: A Phone Call About Deleting the Apps for Good
script: Nadia: [anxious] I actually did it, Reza. I deleted the apps this morning, and now I'm sitting here not knowing what to do with my hands.
Reza: [encouraging] That's honestly a huge step. How are you feeling, beyond the restlessness?
Nadia: [candid] Weirdly bereft, if I'm being fully honest, like I've lost access to a room I used to duck into whenever a conversation got even slightly uncomfortable.
Reza: [understanding] That tracks with what I felt too, when I did this last year. The apps weren't really about entertainment for me, they were an escape hatch from anything remotely difficult.
Nadia: [worried] Did the restlessness ever fully go away, or does it just get quieter over time?
Reza: [honest] It gets quieter, though it never entirely disappears. Even now, my thumb occasionally reaches for a phone that isn't holding the apps anymore, out of pure muscle memory.
Nadia: [frustrated] I keep second-guessing whether this is even proportionate. It's not as if I have some dramatic addiction, I just used them more than I was comfortable admitting.
Reza: [firm] You don't need a dramatic crisis to justify a boundary, Nadia. Noticing discomfort with a habit is reason enough to change it, regardless of how it compares to someone else's story.
Nadia: [relieved] I needed to hear that, honestly. I think I've been waiting for permission from some imagined authority on what counts as a real enough problem.
Reza: [warmly] There isn't an authority handing out permission slips for that. You're allowed to decide something isn't serving you without first proving it nearly ruined your life.
Nadia: [thoughtful] What did you replace the time with, once the initial restlessness settled down?
Reza: [reflective] Nothing dramatic, honestly, mostly just longer, uninterrupted conversations and a considerable amount of staring out of windows, which I'd apparently forgotten how to tolerate.
Nadia: [amused] Staring out of windows sounds suspiciously like something our grandparents would recommend unironically.
Reza: [laughing] They were apparently onto something the whole time. Call me again tonight if the restlessness spikes. I mean that seriously.
Nadia: [grateful] I will. Thank you for not making this sound more dramatic or more trivial than it actually is.
